title: How Does Online Lending Influence Bankruptcy Filings?
near_miss_reason: Every reported DiD column (Tables 4-9) includes five time-varying county controls (population, employment, monthly earnings, median household income, labor force) and uses coarsened-exact-matching weights [aweight=cem_weights]; no controls-free column is reported.
eligible_reason: Design qualifies: county-quarter panel 2008Q1-2014Q4 with binary lending_club_available switching on when the state approves Lending Club (5 adoption cohorts in the all-state sample: 2009Q1, 2011Q1, 2013Q1, 2013Q2, 2014Q3; 289 never-treated counties; no switch-off), county FE and quarter FE. But all columns add time-varying controls and CEM weights (matching-based reweighting is excluded under Section 5b), so the paper is a near-miss.
design_notes: Stata code is given only in readme.pdf (no .do files). Table 4: xtreg bankruptcy_per_capita (and log_bankruptcy) lending_club_available + 5 controls + i.new_timeperiod [aweight=cem_weights], fe cluster(county_code); columns 1-2 all-state matched sample (all_state_replication_data.csv, 2,309 counties), columns 3-4 nine-state sample (339 counties, 3 cohorts). Table 5: leads/lags event study (relative_time_m8andbeyond ... p8andbeyond, m1 omitted) with the same controls and weights. Table 6: non-business vs business bankruptcy. Table 7: interaction with internet access. Table 8: 2011 and 2013 single-cohort subsamples. Table 9: Prosper availability. Tables 10-12: state-level IV (excluded). Data: Federal Judicial Center / AO courts bankruptcy filings, Census, BLS; all CSVs present.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: all-state sample first-treated quarter counts: 5:1720, 13:185, 21:29, 22:30, 27:56 counties; nine-state sample: 13:132, 21:9, 22:14
